notes.reason: Sabine is summarising the Pentagon report in her own voice, not quoting someone she disputes: she says the Pentagon 'couldn't come up with any plausible explanation', that 'they couldn't explain it with any of their own technologies, either, like infrared weapons which they tested in the area at the time', and 'so, they don't know what it is'. I read the actual AARO memorandum (Western U.S. Event 'Orbs Launching Orbs', 05 June 2026, signed by AARO director Jon T. Kosloski) and every quote the note was accepted on appears in it word for word. The memo rates 'Military Aircraft Dispensing Flares' as partially plausible, says flight logs confirm U.S. military aircraft in the area actively deployed infrared countermeasure flares during a standard exercise, that the reported shape and behaviour align with known characteristics of certain military infrared flares, and that radar and ADS-B data suggest approximately 60 percent of the reported activity is plausibly attributable to military aircraft, with about 40 percent left unresolved. So the specific sentence the note is attached to is wrong: the Pentagon did explain most of the sightings with its own technology, and the only hypothesis it actually ruled out was aircraft exhaust. This matters to the video's point, because the whole setup is that the case is a complete mystery that invites Avi Loeb's warp-drive paper. The note does leave out that the agents themselves said the objects did not look like flares and that the case as a whole is officially still unresolved, but it never claims otherwise, and a physicist who is this careful about what reports actually say will most likely welcome a correction that points back at the mundane explanation in the primary document.
